Download standalone edition gave openlaw-documentation.tar.gz (444160 bytes), and Open standalone edition served /documentation-export/index.html ("Documentation · OpenLaw"). The archive extracted outside the instance. In an offline browser context from file://, the index, the Reference and troubleshooting section and the support article read with JavaScript and without it; without JavaScript the index showed the search notice. Signed out, Edition details showed Supported app 0.1.0 / 067c1646829df85e62b809ee9157921e867c84e7 and Distribution commit ad345da5842c22b7d1012bf9f5d7d12dfdb4e496, and /api/v1/meta answered {"name":"OpenLaw","version":"0.1.0"}. The lab's build record named source ad345da5842c22b7d1012bf9f5d7d12dfdb4e496, app image sha256:88db6b8c6ba01c7c7ec9404d795716a9589e112fd369fabc03a76fe292fff9a3 and engine image sha256:eafd797fd144d1fc296b91ac3f81a5407f0626ab2afcdabbc4b38481322136c7, so the installed build comes from the operator's records, not from the version or from Supported app, as the guide says. All 10 internal link targets in the reviewed versions-and-support bytes and all 24 in the troubleshooting bytes opened in the formal reader.

limitations: Independent agent walkthrough by a different agent from the source-review author; not a human user study and not feature-owner approval.

The lab serves the article bytes committed at ad345da5, which still read "The package version alone is insufficient for development builds: different builds can share 0.0.1." The reviewed bytes read "... different development builds can share one version, such as `0.1.0`." Steps followed the reviewed bytes against the app; reader checks prove the routes, headings and UI behavior, and the link checks opened every internal link of the reviewed bytes in the bundled formal reader.

The final lab's Help bundle comes from dev's own edition.json, so Edition details showed Supported app "0.1.0 / 067c1646829df85e62b809ee9157921e867c84e7", not the re-pinned ad345da5. Distribution commit showed ad345da5. The guide makes no claim about the specific values, and the running app reported version 0.1.0 on /api/v1/meta, which matches the example in the changed sentence.

Supported app showed a recorded build, so the Not yet verified value and the Working changes marker were not observed. The Unverified article badge and the development preview notice were not shown; the Validation in progress badge was.
operator is a responsibility, not an OpenLaw account. Operator steps ran signed out, and the build record came from lab.mjs status and docker inspect.
The offline check used an offline browser context and file:// loading of the extracted export while the lab kept running. It did not stop the lab.
The external failure was a browser-blocked github.com request, not a real outage. No GitHub issue was opened.

The walkthrough created only records named DOC-032 support V-C51 ... and changed no organisation settings. The fixture set is the bridge replay's; only the Confidential Contract is used by the V section.
